reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap way places a data center named Set in Dueville, Italy, but records nothing about its operator, size, or power draw.

The entry's substantive content is a name, a coordinate, and a tag. The name is a short generic word that could be an abbreviation, an acronym, or a fragment of a longer business name. There is no operator, no website, and no confirmed Italian business registration. The capacity field reads zero, which here means unrecorded rather than zero megawatts. What the record documents is that a facility is mapped, not what it is.

For AI specifically, this says nothing about compute. A data center tag is a building classification, not a measure of servers, cooling, or grid load. The chain from power to buildings to compute cannot be traced through this entry because no power figure exists in it. The nearest airport, Padova Gino Allegri Airfield at 21.6 miles, is the only other location reference and carries no implication about the facility itself.

What remains unknown is whether the site is active, how large it is, what it draws from the grid, and whether it serves AI workloads at all. Vicenza and the surrounding Veneto region host a mix of light-industrial and small technology businesses, so a small IT operation is plausible, but the data does not confirm it. The honest reading is one mapped point, unconfirmed.
